subject: Re: AzuraMed - DPF evidence & DPA annex clarifications
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@azuramed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Intake <legal@azuramed.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPF questions and evidence list

Sean — thanks for the demo last week. Legal and procurement asked me to collect the following from Redwood to close our security/compliance gate: (1) short DPF mapping that shows where AzuraMed customer data would be stored and which subprocessors handle exports, (2) proposed DPA annex redlines for cross-border transfers (we prefer SCCs + technical measures), and (3) any SOC 2 / penetration test evidence and data-retention controls. Can you confirm you can produce these items by COB Thursday?

We also have a couple of specific questions: Are backups ever stored outside of customer region? Do you support customer-managed KMS?

Appreciate it — Emily
Emily Zhao
Sr. Procurement Manager, AzuraMed

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@azuramed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPF questions and evidence list

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick confirm: we can get a DPF mapping, a proposed DPA annex with SCC language incorporated, and our SOC 2 Type II report extract. Answering your quick Qs up front: backups are by default geo-redundant in the same major cloud region (we replicate across AZs within the region); we do not send backups to other legal jurisdictions unless a customer requests cross-region replication. We do support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in Dedicated/Private deployments; Hosted customers can use our KMS integration with Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) support on enterprise plans.

I'll attach a one-page DPF summary and the draft annex for your legal team to review. Rachel, Marissa — tagging you for technical/ops language and evidence.

Next step: Emily, is AzuraMed aligned to the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or do you accept the new DPF plus SCCs? Happy to align to your preferred mechanism.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPF questions and evidence list

Adding technical clarifications to include in the response pack. I'll prepare the following as separate attachments to keep things audit-friendly: 1) Transfer impact assessment summary (highlighting legal basis and countries of processing), 2) Subprocessors list (current as of 2028-03-20 with roles), 3) Encryption and key management overview (BYOK, HSM options, KMS regions), 4) Backup/replication policy (retention windows and geographic controls), 5) Logging/audit retention (SIEM and retention periods).

Notes to include in DPF mapping: production inference runs in us-west-2 by default for AzuraMed unless you opt for eu-west-1; KV caches are ephemeral and keys are not persisted outside the serving cluster. For Hosted customers we anonymize telemetry; for Dedicated/Private we can switch off telemetry collection and offer private telemetry sinks.

I'll draft the TIA summary and a concise evidence index. Marissa: can you add customer success notes about retention / deletion workflow?

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Security & Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@azuramed.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AzuraMed - DPF evidence & DPA annex clarifications

Emily — attaching the operational answers to complement Rachel's technical pack. Key items: 1) Data retention: default 90 days for inference logs, 30 days for raw prompts/traces for hosted unless a custom retention policy is set; AzuraMed can request shorter retention or immediate purge for PII via API call. 2) Deletion workflow: we support per-customer purge requests with a documented runbook and verification logs. 3) Access controls: RBAC + SSO (SAML/OIDC) with audit trails; we provide exportable audit logs for the retention period. 4) Incident response: 24/7 on-call and SOC playbook — we can share a redacted runbook.

Attachment stubs: redwood-dpf-summary-20280320.pdf, dpa-annex-draft-azuramed-20280321.docx.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@azuramed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Intake <legal@azuramed.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@azuramed.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AzuraMed - DPF evidence & DPA annex clarifications

Thanks — the pack looks promising. A few clarifying asks from legal/IT after a quick read-through: 1) In the DPA annex we need explicit language about emergency cross-border access requests and a process for customer approval; can Redwood commit to 48-hour notice and customer approval for access unless there's a lawful request? 2) Can you confirm that telemetry data used for model-quality and product analytics is pseudonymized and never linked to AzuraMed's user identifiers? 3) Procurement wants a short statement of any cross-border subprocessors that can access customer data in EU or APAC jurisdictions.

Also, please confirm the date you can provide a redacted SOC 2 report and the latest penetration test summary.

—Emily

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@azuramed.com>, Legal Intake <legal@azuramed.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AzuraMed - DPF evidence & DPA annex clarifications

Emily — great questions. Quick answers and commitments: 1) Emergency cross-border access: Redwood's default process is to notify and obtain customer approval for any access to production datasets by staff in other jurisdictions; we are willing to add explicit 48-hour notice language into the annex with an exception only for lawful process (we will provide notice as permitted). 2) Telemetry: confirmed — telemetry used for product analytics is pseudonymized at ingest and kept separate from AzuraMed identifiers; we will add a short appendix describing the pseudonymization steps (salted hashing + tokenization) and retention. 3) Subprocessors with potential cross-border access: (a) Cloud provider (AWS) — compute in us-west-2, eu-west-1; (b) Observability vendor (LogSinkCo) — log ingestion in us-west-2 with EU processing options on request; (c) VectorDB partner (SearchGrid) — optional, only used if customer enables advanced reranking; we will provide a signed subprocessors attestation.

SOC 2: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report by Friday 2028-03-24 and a penetration test executive summary by the same date. I'll push the annex update (add 48-hour clause + telemetry appendix) and share for legal redlines.

Please let me know if AzuraMed needs any SLA or retention updates for the draft.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199
